The interior of the _Celebrity Big Brother_ house has a New York City theme from around the 1940s.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-House-6-57) Each of the bedrooms on the first floor were given their own individual names reflecting their design. The first bedroom has a "5th Avenue" theme inspired by window shopping highlighting "the highest fashion of the '40s" while the second bedroom has a luxury "Hotel" theme. The third bedroom, known as the "Celebrity Building" Bedroom, that was inspired by a famous art deco building named after a car company.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-House-3-54) The kitchen was inspired by some of the finest restaurants in New York City with a "faux French" oven island and a square dining room table. Behind the dining room table cartoon-style pictures of the season one HouseGuests hanging on the wall.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-House-6-57) The bathroom and downstairs lounge area were inspired by the 20th Century Limited passenger train.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-House-4-55) The Head of Household bedroom resembles the backstage of a Broadway show with the head board made from a real theater marquee.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-House-5-56) The upstairs lounge was designed after the Brooklyn Bridge, while the gym area was inspired by the 42nd Street library in Manhattan.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-House-Twitter-58)

The main television coverage of the second season was screened on CBS during the winter of the 2018–19 network television season. The season premiere was on January 21, 2019, with the season finale airing on February 13, 2019.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-CBB2-Schedule-59) Alongside the weekly shows on CBS, the companion series _Celebrity Big Brother: After Dark_ returned on Pop and to provide live coverage nightly from inside the House.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-60)
The format remains largely unchanged from the previous season. HouseGuests are incarcerated in the Big Brother House with no contact to and from the outside world. Periodically, the HouseGuests take part in several compulsory challenges that determine who would win safety and power in the House.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-format-ep1-61) The winner of the Head of Household (HoH) competition is immune from nominations and is instructed to nominate two fellow HouseGuests for eviction.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Format-1-62) After a HouseGuest became Head of Household, he or she was ineligible to take part in the next Head of Household competition. The winner of the Power of Veto competition wins the right to save one of the nominated HouseGuests from eviction.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Format-1-62) If the Veto winner exercised the power, the Head of Household then had to nominate another HouseGuest for eviction.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Format-1-62)

On eviction night, all HouseGuests except for the Head of Household and the nominees voted to evict one of the nominees.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Format-1-62) Before the voting began, the nominees had the chance to say a final message to their fellow HouseGuests.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Format-1-62) This compulsory vote is conducted in the privacy of the Diary Room by the host Julie Chen Moonves. In the event of a tie, the Head of Household would break the tie and reveal their vote in front of the other HouseGuests.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Format-1-62) Unlike other versions of _Big Brother_, the HouseGuests can discuss the nomination and eviction process open and freely.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-63)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-64) The nominee with the most votes from the other HouseGuests is evicted from the House on eviction night and interviewed by the host.

HouseGuests can voluntarily leave the House at any time (referred to as "walking") and those who break the rules are expelled by Big Brother.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Walking-example-65)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Expelled-example-66) The evictees of the season form the Jury that vote for the winner on the season finale; they are known as the jury members.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-Format-Jury-67) Unlike the jury members of _Big Brother_, the celebrity jury members are not sequestered after their eviction and are able to watch the show after their eviction.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-format-ep13-68) The winner of _Celebrity Big Brother_ receives the grand prize of $250,000.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_2_(American_season)#cite_note-CastPR-53)

_**Celebrity Big Brother**_, also known as _**Big Brother: Celebrity Edition**_, is a reality televisionspin-off series of the American adaptation of _Big Brother_ created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") The series began on February 7, 2018, on CBS in the United States and is simulcast in Canada on Global. The series is filmed at CBS Studio Center in sound stage eighteen located in Studio City, Los Angeles. Julie Chen Moonves reprises her role as host from _Big Brother_ with Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan also returning as executive producers. The series is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.
The premise of the series remained largely unchanged from the main edition of _Big Brother_, in which a group of contestants, known as "HouseGuests," who live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother House, with no contact from the outside world. The contestants compete in competitions for safety and for power over the household before voting each other out in an attempt to be the last HouseGuest remaining and win a grand prize. The difference from the parent series is the inclusion of "Celebrity" HouseGuests (those with notoriety prior to participating in the series), the time frame (a month as opposed to 3 months) and a smaller grand prize ($250,000 as opposed to $750,000)
Each season is also transmitted in real-time which allows for greater viewer participation in the form of _America's Vote_ where the public can give their favorite HouseGuest various prizes ranging from luxury items to advantage to help them survive inside the House. Prior to the live season finale, the viewers are able to vote for their _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with the winner getting an auxiliary prize of $25,000.

The first overall season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ worldwide premiered in the United Kingdom in 2001 while an American version of the format has been speculated since 2002. The first season of the American adaptation was announced during a live double eviction episode of the nineteenth regular season on September 7, 2017, by Julie Chen Moonves. The first season was scheduled during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The series premiere was the number one program for CBS attracting 7.27 million viewers and the highest-rated season premiere since _Big Brother 13_. The program was often covered in the media due to the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her political revelations in the first season.
In September 2021, CBS renewed _Celebrity Big Brother_ for a third season, which premiered on February 2, 2022.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Air_date-1)
In October 2025, CBS cancelled _Celebrity Big Brother_ after three seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-2)

The series is a game show in which a group of celebrity contestants, referred to as HouseGuests, live in a custom-built set, known as the Big Brother House, constantly under video surveillance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3) While in the House, the HouseGuests are completely isolated from the outside world, meaning no phone, television, Internet, magazines, newspaper, or contact with those not in the House.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) This rule could be broken, however, in the event of a medical injury, a family emergency, or death.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) The format of the series is mainly seen as a social experiment, and requires HouseGuests to interact with others who may have differing ideals, beliefs, and prejudices.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3.2-6) Though locked in the House, the HouseGuests are free to quit the game, though will not be allowed entry back into the game.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-4-7) Should a HouseGuest break the rules of the game, they could be expelled from the House,

and unable to return.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-5-8) The HouseGuests compete for a grand prize of $250,000 and the runner-up is awarded $50,000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9) Prior to the live finale the viewers are able to award their favorite HouseGuest of the season the title _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with a cash prize of $25,000.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9)

### Differences from _Big Brother_
Deena Katz serves as the casting director for the series she also is known for casting ABC's _Dancing with the Stars_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Casting-42) Grodner revealed she spoke with the producers of the British adaptation about their experiences with celebrities. Due to the American adaptation featuring more competitions than other formats there is no special treatment for the celebrities in order for the competitions "to be as fair as possible".[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-43)Tamar Braxton won the second season and became the first ever African-American HouseGuest to win in the history of the American adaptation of _Big Brother_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB2_Winner-22) In an effort to promote diversity, CBS announced a new rule for _Big Brother_ that 50% of all contestants must be a person of color or an indigenous person for the 2021–2022 broadcast season.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-19 "Big Brother (American TV series)")

### Production design and music
[edit]
_Celebrity Big Brother_ uses a similar title sequence and logo that was introduced with the sixteenth season of _Big Brother_ that was designed by Charlie Co.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Graphics-1-44) The logo was slightly modified to remove the water effects which were replaced by faint lights while the word "Celebrity" before "Big" with "Brother" underneath. The water effect that was used as a transition and appears around the HouseGuests was removed. This was replaced with a star being used as the transition and items related to the celebrities notoriety appeared around them.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-BB19Opening-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB1Opening-46) The series also uses the same theme song as _Big Brother_ during the opening title sequence which was composed by David Vanacore and Ken Berry.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-ClosingCredits-36)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-BB19Opening-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB1Opening-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-47)
A view of CBS Studio Center sound stage 18, where the house is located

### Production design and music
Filming for the series takes place at CBS Studio Center, sound stage eighteen where the sitcom _Yes, Dear_ was filmed.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-House-1-48)_Celebrity Big Brother_ is filmed in the same location as _Big Brother_ since its sixth season and is referred to as the _Big Brother House_ often shortened to _House_.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-House-2-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-House-3-50) The House has 94 high-definition cameras and over 113 microphones in order to monitor and record the HouseGuests.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBS-CBB2-PR-51) The first floor of the House consists of three bedrooms, storage room and the Diary Room which is accessible by the living room. The bathroom, a lounge room, backyard and a spiral staircase going to the second floor are accessed via the kitchen. The front door is located in a vestibule area that separates the living room and kitchen. The Head of Household bedroom and en suite bathroom is located on the second floor. The second floor also has a balcony with an additional lounge area where the HouseGuests can look down and see the first floor. The backyard is significantly smaller due to the majority of the backyard being used for constant competitions.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-House-4-52) During _Celebrity Big Brother_ a roof is installed over the backyard.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-53) The pool table was brought inside from the backyard and moved to the upstairs lounge area.

### Production design and music
The spare room sometimes used for tasks on the civilian _Big Brother_ series, such as the Den of Temptation in season nineteen, is turned into an indoor gym for the celebrity edition.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-CBB1-House-54)
After the success of the first season CBS ordered a second season to air during the winter of the 2018–19 television season on May 12, 2018.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-55) The network reconfirmed the news four days later when the network revealed its 2018–19 fall prime-time schedule.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-56) After the departure of Les Moonves from CBS Corporation on September 9, 2018, because of multiple sexual misconduct allegations, the media speculated that Julie Chen Moonves might not continue hosting _Celebrity Big Brother_ and _Big Brother_.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-57) CBS later confirmed on November 27, 2018 that Chen Moonves would host the second season of the series.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-JCReturn-35)

### Production design and music
_Celebrity Big Brother_ was not mentioned when CBS announced their plans for the 2019–20 television season on May 15, 2019.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-59)Kelly Kahl, president of entertainment at CBS, revealed on May 21, 2019 that a third season of the celebrity spin-off is still uncertain.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-60) On September 5, 2019 the parent series _Big Brother_ was renewed for a twenty-second season with Chen Moonves signing a new contract to return as host.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-61) However the new contract for Chen Moonves did not include a future season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ with CBS not announcing anything official regarding the series.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-62) On November 11, 2019, CBS announced their 2020 winter schedule, which did not include _Celebrity Big Brother_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-63) On December 28, 2020, Chen Moonves revealed that shortly after the conclusion of the twenty-second season of the civilian version of _Big Brother_ that she and numerous producers pushed CBS to order a third season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ but that they declined to order one at the time leaving the option open to still order a third season at a later date.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-64)
